newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols skid, call buying up.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols skid, call buying up.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options sank Friday, as expected after the May employment report, while investment firms bought July calls amid an explosive rally in futures, traders said.

September volatility was quoted at 7.75 percent at the close after starting the day at 9.00 percent. July dropped to 7.30 percent after hovering around 7.50 percent for most of the day, but traders cautioned that reading was growing less relevant with the options approaching expiration in about two weeks.
Meanwhile, futures staged a furious advance on a combination of technical bullishness and fundamental rumors that overshadowed the uncertain implications of the jobs data.

September bond futures settled 1 7/32 higher at 111-07, near the day's high and at the highest level seen since February. The contract midmorning burst through stubborn resistance at 110-03 to 110-09 after several failed attempts earlier in the week.
Feeding the rally were an array of rumors suggesting Asian central bank buying, a deal in European monetary union and the cancellation of some 10-year Treasury note auctions.
The Labor Department this morning said the U.S. economy added just 138,000 nonfarm payroll jobs in May, but it also revised April payrolls up sharply to 323,000 and adjusted March higher as well.

In bond options, floor traders said one U.S. house bought 5,000 July 111-00 calls when they were out of the money and a second house bought 2,000 of the 112-00 calls as bullish momentum swelled. Market participants also sold puts early in the session and were later seen buying them back.
Eurodollar volatility was unchanged for a second day, at 9.0 percent for September options and 10.9 percent for December.
